Everything lives in folders. Pick a folder at the top, then tap New note. The gear at the top opens settings, the arrow icon imports a note from a file. The title of a new note is already filled in with its kind and the next free number in the folder (Audio 1, Budget 2…): tap Create at once and rename it later, or type your own name. A new folder is named the same way: Folder 1, Folder 2… (Tasks 1… for a folder of tasks); Create works at once, and the name can be changed then or later. Many buttons are icons: press and hold an icon to see its name (TalkBack reads it too). Buttons of dialogs, rare and irreversible actions keep their words.

A folder groups notes and has a name, colour and style. Every note is in exactly one folder, and the last folder cannot be deleted. When you delete a folder you choose whether its notes move to another folder or go with it. A folder\'s card has a small row of buttons at the top — select, drag to move, and the ⋮ menu — then its icon and name, its note count and, if switched on in Settings, its creation and change stamps.

There are eleven kinds of notes: note (formatted text), Markdown, list, budget, drawing, blueprint, audio, photo, camera video, screen recording and schedule. Tap a note to open it; changes are saved automatically. The ⋮ menu on a card pins it (the note pinned last is on top), makes its title bold, adds a comment or tags, sets a colour or a reminder, clones, moves or deletes it. Deleted notes can be restored right after with Undo. In a Markdown note, a list and a budget the magnifier at the top finds words inside the note: every match is marked, “3 / 7” counts them, the arrows go to the previous and the next one (a budget opens the groups that hold one), the cross closes the search. While a long list or text scrolls, two round buttons appear at the bottom right: to the beginning and to the end (in the notes of a folder, in every note, and in the Edit of a long text). New folder asks its kind: a folder of notes or a folder of tasks. In a folder of tasks “New” makes a task: a name, a comment, a start and an end, a “Done” tick and a description, all changed on its Edit tab, where “Reminder…” sets its reminders. A task whose end has passed and that is not done is marked “Overdue”; the calendar shows every task as a bar from its start to its end. At the top of an open note two icons switch it: the open book is View (read the note, nothing changes by a stray tap), the pencil on a line is Edit (change it); the chosen one is highlighted, and a long press on an icon shows its name.

A budget is a tree. An item holds a sum and a goal that you type. A group adds up its items automatically, and groups can contain groups. Remainder is goal minus sum and may be negative (shown in red). Tap ▾ to collapse a group. “Display options” lets you put the overall total and the group totals at the bottom and list the newest items first; each budget remembers its own choice. Each item also has a small +/− “Change the sum” button, in View and in Edit alike, to quickly add or subtract an amount instead of retyping the whole sum; in Edit its ⋮ menu also has Edit for the full dialog (name, sum, goal, quantity, comment, group) besides Add item, Add group and Delete. In the Change dialog the buttons +, − and = add, subtract or put in the amount; the Sum and Goal switches choose what changes — the sum (at first), the goal, or both at once (one of them always stays on). Kind (in Edit): Account, Income or Expense. An income or expense is merged once into the chosen account — its sums are added (income) or subtracted (expense) — at the set date and time, shown in the calendar with 💰, or at once with “Merge now”. Ticks: Sums, Goals, Same items (add into the item of the same name, or of the same group/item path — the switch under the ticks) and Transfer all items (the others are created in the account). With no account chosen nothing happens. After the merge the income / expense goes to the trash and can be restored; the account’s log has “Undo the merge”. The Change dialog also has an optional comment: it is written into the log line of that change. Edit → Display → Hide sums / Hide goals: the amounts show as stars on the card, in the note and in its log (the remainder too when either is hidden); the eye beside View / Edit shows them until the note is closed. Export and Share keep the numbers. The icons above the budget: the clock with an arrow opens the log, the sliders open the display options (in Edit), the two arrows together and apart close and open all groups. In the log a change of an item (its sum, goal, quantity, name) or an added item or group has Undo: the change is taken back by its own difference, so what was done after it stays; an added item is deleted again (you are asked first). Each line can be undone once. An income and an expense have no goal and no remainder, only sums. The eye of the note and of every line works in View and in Edit. In Edit the ⋮ menu of an item has “Merge into another item…”: the item is deleted, and the item you choose gets its sum, its goal or both. In View every item and every group has a bin icon — Delete (you are asked first). What was deleted stays in the log: its line “Deleted” has Restore, which puts the item or the group back with everything that was inside it, into its group — or under the total when that group is gone. A deletion is restored once.

A schedule is a list of rows: items (a time of day, once you set it, a description and a comment) and calculators (the time between two chosen items, under a description of their own — handy for a shift length or a wait). Add either kind with the + button. Drag rows by the grip for your own order, or use Sort to arrange items by time or by name; calculators always come after the items, and Manual brings your own order back. In Edit the clock with a plus adds a time, the calculator adds a calculator, and the speech bubble with a plus adds a comment to a line.

Draw with a finger on two layers. The RASTER layer has a pencil, a brush, an eraser and a bucket fill; the VECTOR layer on top holds lines, arrows, rectangles, ellipses, triangles and free-hand pen shapes that you can select, move, reshape, fill, reorder and delete. Each layer can be hidden. The picture is saved automatically. Export it as PNG or JPEG (both layers merged), or as Layers to keep the shapes editable, from the ⋮ menu.

Markdown notes use the Markdown syntax. The toolbar adds bold, italic, headings, lists, checklists, quotes, code and links; press Enter at the end of a list item to continue the list. Switch to Preview to read the formatted note and tick checklist boxes. In View a checklist line can also be dragged by its four-arrow grip among the lines of its own level, with the lines under it, and deleted with the bin button (it asks first); Undo takes both back.

Tap Record and allow the microphone once; tap Stop to finish. Each recording is added to the list of this note. Play any of them and drag its slider to move around. In a recording\'s ⋮ menu give it a name and a comment, export it as a .m4a file or delete it; the other recordings stay. The ⋮ menu of the note exports all recordings as one .zip, each file named “note title - recording name”. Every recording stops by itself after a time limit and is saved: 4 minutes by default, set for audio, camera video and screen recording in Settings → Recordings (0 = until you press Stop); the note shows the limit under the Record button and says it when the recording starts. Stop still works earlier.

Settings has Export all data and Import all data: one file with everything, to move to another phone or keep safe. On import choose Merge (keep both), Add as new copies, or Replace everything. A single note is exported from its ⋮ menu (Markdown, JSON, PNG, JPEG or audio) and imported with the arrow icon on the main screen. Files from newer versions of the app are refused with a message, never half-imported.

Notes stay on your phone; there is no cloud sync. Backups contain no passwords. Reminder notifications show generic text by default; you can change that in Settings. A note, a Markdown note, a list, a drawing and a blueprint can hide their content: open the note, go to Edit and press the crossed eye in the row of the tabs. After that the card and View show “The content is hidden” until you press the eye; closed and opened again, the note is hidden again. The title, the tags and the comment stay visible, and search still finds the words. It is a cover against a glance, not a lock: the app lock is what keeps a stranger out. Photo, video and audio notes have no such option. Several notes at once: in a folder press Select, tick the notes and press the crossed eye in the bar at the bottom to hide their content, or the eye to stop hiding it; the number on the icon says how many notes change. Photo, video and audio notes among them stay as they are, and Undo in the message turns the change back.
Folder: a named group of notes.
Note: one text, list, budget, drawing or audio item that lives in a folder.
Group: a budget entry made of other entries; its sum and goal are added up automatically.
Item: a budget entry with its own sum and goal that you type.
Goal: the amount you plan to reach or spend.
Remainder: goal minus sum. Negative means the goal is exceeded.
Backup: a file with all your data, used to restore or move it.
Deleted notes and folders wait here until you restore them or delete them for good.
Items stay here until you restore them or empty the trash.

How long deleted notes and folders are kept before they are removed for good.

Deleted notes and folders go to the trash (the bin button at the top of the main screen), where you can restore them or delete them for good; every permanent deletion asks for confirmation. The trash empties itself only if you choose so in Settings → Trash (7 to 90 days); by default it never does, so nothing disappears by surprise. A note whose folder is also in the trash is restored into a folder you choose. Photos, videos and recordings you delete from a note go to the trash too: from there they can be put back into the note, exported as a file or deleted for good; if the note itself is gone, they can only be exported. The magnifier at the top finds things in the trash: names of folders, notes and items, the text of notes, the notes that went with a folder and the comments of items; the words are marked, a piece of the text is shown, the arrows go from one to the next. Each item has icons: the arrow out of the bin restores it, the bin with a cross deletes it for good (you are asked first), the arrow down saves a deleted photo or recording to a file.

A list has items with a check box, an optional quantity, a unit and a comment. Add a “unit total” to see the sum of the quantities of all items in one unit, for example the kilograms of everything on the list; you can have several totals with different units. Units are managed in Settings: pieces, kilograms, litres, metres, roubles, dollars, pounds and euros are built in and cannot be deleted; you can add your own. Each item also has small +/− “Change” buttons for its quantity and its price (Enter overwrites the number instead), and its ⋮ menu has Edit for the full dialog with all its fields. In Edit the list with a plus adds an item and the sum sign Σ adds a total by unit.

resources.string: “%1$s” goes to the trash; you can put it back into this note from there.
Add quantities and prices to see the totals.

In a list, open the Edit tab and choose Prices instead of Quantities. Each item then also has a price of one and a unit for the price, chosen from the same units as quantities (roubles, euros, even kilograms). The cost of an item is quantity × price: 2 apples at 50 make 100. At the end the list adds up all quantities per unit and all costs per price unit, for example 5 pcs and 400 rub. A “unit total” row also shows the cost of the items in its unit.

The magnifier at the top of the main screen opens search. Switch between Notes (looks in titles, text and tags of notes in all folders) and Folders (finds a folder by name). Several words must all be found. Under the search field, tap tags to keep only the notes that have all of them. To tag a note, use its ⋮ menu → Tags: tick tags or type a new one; a note can have any number of tags. Settings → Manage tags renames or deletes a tag.

Open a note and use its ⋮ menu → Export. Markdown notes: Markdown (with the syntax), plain text or PDF (both show the text as you read it). Lists: their own JSON file (comes back with all quantities and prices), Markdown, plain text or PDF. Budgets, drawings and audio have their own formats. Audio notes with several recordings export them all in one .zip, named “note title - recording name”; a single recording is exported from its own ⋮ menu.

A drawing is a sheet you paint on: pencil, brush, eraser, bucket fill, any colour. A blueprint is made of shapes (the Shapes tool: rectangle, square, ellipse, circle, triangle, rhombus, pentagon, hexagon, star, line, arrows; filled or not; and texts) that you can select, move, reshape and fill, and they sit on layers. In Edit tap “Layers”: choose the layer to draw on, hide or lock a layer, move it up or down, rename or delete it, add a new one; a shape can be moved to another layer from the ⋮ menu of that layer. A drawing made in an older version keeps its shapes, but they can only be seen now, not changed. Both open in View first; zoom with the + and − buttons or two fingers, and move the zoomed sheet with two fingers. A selected shape moves one step forward or backward, or straight to the front or to the back; a layer goes one place up or down, or to the very top or bottom. The icon of a half-filled square on the tool panel sets the sheet background: a colour, and Transparent with how see-through it is (100 % = no background). The picture is saved and shared with this background. A chosen shape has icons: the bin deletes it, two sheets duplicate it, the layered squares move it one step forward or back, the arrows to a line move it to the very front or back. A layer shows an eye (shown / hidden) and a lock (locked / free); the stack with a plus adds a layer.

Text, list and budget notes have − and + buttons at the top, next to View and Edit, and zoom by pinching with two fingers: it makes the letters bigger or smaller in that note; tap the percentage to go back to normal. Drawings and blueprints zoom the sheet itself with the same buttons. The zoom is kept while you stay on the note. For the whole app choose a size in Settings → Appearance → Font size; it is added to the font size of the system settings. A drawing or blueprint sheet lies in the whole note; pinch or − / + zoom it, smaller than the area too, and two fingers move it; a tap on the zoom level fits the whole sheet into the free part. In Edit the tool panel lies over the sheet, at the bottom or on the right (the frame icon on the panel switches), and the arrow icon folds it into one round button; the sheet never covers the buttons. The frame icon on the tool panel sets the size of the sheet: 16:9, 9:16, 4:3, 3:4 or any width and height in px, mm or cm (150 pixels per inch); the picture stays at the top left. The frame icon with a band on the tool panel chooses where the panel lies: at the bottom, on the right, at the top or on the left; the choice is kept.

The ⋮ menu at the top of the main screen has Sort: notes by change date, creation date, name or colour, folders by your own order, name, dates or colour, each ascending or descending. Pinned notes always stay first, the one pinned last on top. With “My order” you drag folders and notes by the four-arrow grip; the ⋮ menu of a folder card also moves it earlier or later. Each folder remembers its own sort of notes.

Settings → Backgrounds lets you give the whole app, the folder cards and each kind of note a colour or a PNG/JPG picture from your phone. A picture is dimmed a little so text stays readable; a plain colour is used as it is, so pick one that suits the text (Reset brings the default back). Pictures stay on this phone and are not part of a backup; colours are.

The clock icon at the top of the main screen (or “Reminders” in a note’s ⋮ menu) opens the reminders. Add one: choose the note, the day and time, and how it calls for attention: a melody (a phone sound or your own audio file) with a volume and a gradual fade-in, vibration, a pop-up, asking for confirmation, and repeating every few minutes until you confirm. “Repeat like an alarm clock” rings again X more times every N minutes. A reminder can come back every day, on chosen weekdays or on a day of the month (a month without that day is skipped). Edit, cancel or delete a reminder, or tap Done when it waits for confirmation. Android 13 and later asks once to allow notifications; if the phone has not allowed exact alarms a note on the screen explains it and opens the setting, and a reminder may then come a little late. A reminder of a deleted note is cancelled. The calendar icon next to the clock opens a month with a bell on every day that has a reminder (a repeating one on each of its days); tap a day to see the names of its notes in a bubble and in a list under the month, tap a name to open the note. Arrows or a swipe change the month, Today comes back. The magnifier of the calendar finds reminders and budget merges by the note name in every month: the found ones are listed with their dates, a tap or the arrows show that day. A reminder still to ring has an on / off switch on its card: switched off it keeps its time and settings but does not ring; switched on again it comes back (a repeating one at its next day). Cancel asks first. A tap on a reminder notification opens the calendar on that day with the reminder framed; a tap there opens the note or the task. The icons of a reminder card: the tick is Done, the pencil changes it, the crossed-out bell cancels it, the bin deletes it (both ask first). After Notio is installed all reminders are off: turn them on with the switch at the top of the Reminders page; an attempt to add a reminder says so too. A ring that repeats and is not answered lights the screen for less each time: a minute, then 15 seconds, then 5 seconds; the melody plays as usual.

Settings → App lock: choose a password, a 3×3 pattern, or a login with a password. Add fingerprint or face unlocking if the phone has it: it only adds a quicker way, the password or pattern always stays. Choose how long the app may stay in the background before it asks again, from the presets or any minutes and seconds (“Other…”). If you forget the secret, there are three ways to get back in, each optional: answering a security question, a code sent by e-mail through your own SMTP server (the app has no server of its own), or a code from an authenticator app (QR code). Without any of them a forgotten secret cannot be recovered; reinstalling the app is then the only way and it deletes everything on the phone (import a backup file afterwards). After five wrong tries the app makes you wait, longer each time. Only a scrambled (hashed) form of the secret is kept, in the app’s private storage, and never in a backup. While the lock is on, screenshots and the recent-apps picture are blocked. The letter with the recovery code also carries the password of the encrypted database and the password of the backups, if this device has them: the last resort to get the data back. It is sent only when you press “I forgot it” and ask for the code; delete it afterwards.

Three more kinds of notes hold many items each, like an audio note: Photo, Camera video and Screen recording. Every item has a small picture, a name, a comment, the time it was made and changed and, if you asked for it, the place. Tap an item to look at it: photos open full screen (swipe to the next, pinch to zoom), videos play in the note or full screen; the picture follows the turn of the phone. The camera button asks for the camera; choose the back, the front or any other camera the phone has. A video can have no sound, the microphone, the sound the phone itself plays (Android 10 and later) or both. Screen recording: the app steps aside; stop it with the Stop button of the notification or, if you allowed “Display over other apps”, with the small red button over the windows (on some phones that button may show in the recording). “Overlays” lay the date and time, the place, a text (a signature) and a picture (a logo) over every new photo or video: choose the format, colour, size and position, and whether there is a plate behind (off = transparent). Every photo, video and recording goes into a backup, however big; a large backup can take several minutes. Settings → Appearance → “Pictures on cards” chooses whether these notes show a picture on their card in the notes list: none, the first photo or frame, or a fanned stack of up to three; drawings and blueprints have their own separate on/off for their one picture there. A screen recording shows a floating Stop button over other apps; the “Floating Stop button” switch next to the sound choice turns it off; if the phone’s battery settings restrict Notio in the background, a recording stops as soon as you leave the app — the note warns about it and opens those settings (choose “Unrestricted”); without it, stop from the notification. Every recording stops by itself after a time limit and is saved: 4 minutes by default, set for audio, camera video and screen recording in Settings → Recordings (0 = until you press Stop); the note shows the limit under the Record button and says it when the recording starts. Stop still works earlier. A voice or camera recording goes on when the app is minimised or the phone is locked, until Stop — in the note, in the notification or on the red floating button (switch “Floating Stop button”) — or its time limit; a screen recording still ends when the screen is locked. Under the Record button, “Change for this recording” sets a time limit for the next recording only (0 = until Stop); the one after goes by Settings → Recordings again. The checklist icon starts selecting items; while selecting, the icons select all, clear the selection and delete the chosen ones (you are asked first). A clip plays and pauses with the round play button; a video opens full screen with the corners icon.

A Note is formatted text, next to the Markdown notes. Settings → Sync connects two devices with Notio on the same Wi-Fi, directly, without internet or cloud; both keep this page open. The first time, one device presses Wait for a device and shows a code, the other presses Find a device, chooses it (or types its address) and types the code; the first one confirms. The connection is kept in the list: later just press Sync…, choose the direction (from here, to here or both ways), how (Merge — the newer change wins; Add as copies; Replace — the receiver becomes an exact copy, only in one direction; with chosen folders only they are replaced) and all folders or chosen ones; the other device is asked every time. Test connection shows step by step what does not work; Remove breaks the connection. Everything is encrypted (AES-256-GCM, keys by ECDH); the code is never sent over the network. If the Wi-Fi gives the other device a new address (".152" one day, ".153" the next) and it is not found by itself, press Address… on the kept connection and type the address and port it shows at the top of its Sync page. The pairing key does not change: a device at that address without the key is refused. If the network changed while Notio was open (Wi-Fi instead of mobile data or a VPN), press “Check the connections again”: the address of this device and the list of devices nearby are read anew. The port this device listens on is chosen automatically; “Port of this device…” sets your own (for a rule of a firewall or a router) and says whether it is free or taken by another program.

In a folder of tasks every task has a status: Created, Queued, Planned, In work, Paused, Postponed, Waiting, In review, Done, Closed or Cancelled. The status is a button with its icon — on the card of the task, in View and in Edit; press it and choose from the list. Done, Closed and Cancelled end a task: it is no longer overdue. Beside the status is the priority: a whole number from 0 to 65535, digits only, or empty. The sort of a folder of tasks has Status and Priority; the chips above the tasks leave only the tasks of the chosen statuses, and the same chips are in the search of notes. The tick beside the status is “Completed”: it stands on the card of a task, in View and in Edit. Ticked, the task becomes Done; cleared, it gets back the status it had before. The chips “Not completed” and “Completed” above the tasks and in the search of notes leave only such tasks, and the sorting of a folder of tasks has “Completed”: the tasks still open come first. These two chips are icons: an empty box is “Not completed”, a ticked box is “Completed”; the words come up as the hint of the icon. The bin at the end of the line of a task — on its card and in View — deletes the task: it asks first, and the task goes to the trash, from where it can be restored. The two sheets beside it copy the task as text.

An income or an expense is merged into its account at the time set in Edit. Repeat chooses how often: once, every day, every week on chosen days, every month or every year. A merge that repeats stays in its folder and waits for its next time; a month without that day takes its last day; times missed while Notio was closed are merged at the next start. “Merge now” merges at once and does not move the time. Two ticks decide whether the case of names matters: with them “Cash” and “cash” are one item or one group, without them two.

Under the search field (on the main screen and inside a note) there are two ticks.
• Aa any case — on: “tea” finds tea, Tea and TEA; off: only exactly “tea”.
• .* Regexp — off: the words are plain text in which * stands for any characters and ? for exactly one: *Tasty* finds “Tasty soup” (stars at the ends change nothing), Tast* finds Tasty and Taste, t?a finds tea and toa.
On: the words are a regular expression. . any character, .* any characters, \d a digit, \d+ a number, \s a space, ^ the start and $ the end of a line, [abc] one of these letters, a|b one or the other, ( ) a group, \. a real dot.
Examples: ^Buy — lines that start with Buy; \d+ kg — 5 kg, 250 kg; tea|coffee — either; Tast(y|e) — Tasty and Taste.
A wrong expression (for example *Tasty* with Regexp on) finds nothing, and a red line says why. On the main screen without Regexp every word must be found; with Regexp the whole line is one expression.
“%1$s” repeats what stands before it, and there is nothing there. For the sign itself write \\%1$s, for “any characters” write .*

The assistant lets you drive Notio with words through a model that runs on your own computer, for example LM Studio. It is off until you turn it on in Settings → Assistant. Connection: the whole address of the model with its port and, if the server asks, a key; Check shows whether the server answers and which models it has. Rights: what the assistant may do at all — read, create notes, change text, move and sort, move to the trash; nothing is allowed until you tick it. Access to notes: a folder or a note is open to the assistant only when you turn its switch on; a closed one does not exist for it. Apply to all notes sets the choice of a folder for every note in it. The chat is the button at the top of the main screen: write what to do, and under an answer that changed something stands Roll back. The journal keeps every such request with how it was before; Roll back puts the notes back and moves what the assistant made to the trash. The assistant never purges anything, never changes its own rights, the access of notes, the lock or passwords. A model can be wrong, so check what it did. Rights also cover tags, colour and pin, the items of a list, the status and dates of a task, the sums of a budget, reminders, folders, the appearance and some settings of the app. The assistant stops and asks for your yes before it changes more than five notes in one request and before any sum of a budget: press Confirm and continue. The menu of a note and of a folder has Open to the assistant and Close to the assistant. Telegram bot: your own bot that runs inside Notio on this computer. Paste its key from @BotFather, send the bot the code Notio shows, and it listens to you only; give it rights of its own under Rights from Telegram and mark the notes it may see with May go to Telegram. In Telegram, /undo rolls back its last change and /yes confirms. Reminders to Telegram on a note sends the title of the note to the bot when its reminder rings. The words you exchange with the bot pass through the servers of Telegram. Whom the bot listens to is decided by Notio, not by Telegram: the number of the Telegram account that sent the code, which a new name does not change. The code works ten minutes and burns after five wrong tries; New code gives another. The page shows the name and number of the bound account and how many strangers wrote. Rights from Telegram have Allow all and Forbid all. The chat is kept after a restart unless you turn off Keep the chat after a restart. Point the mouse at a message to copy it or delete it; Clear the chat deletes all messages, while the notes and the journal stay. If your own bot program (TelegramBot) already reads the bot, choose Through your bot program: Notio makes a code of 12 characters with Show, Hide, Copy and New code; the admin of the bot enters it in /admin, then Notio; people write /notio with the code, then /n and a request, and the bot answers only the people you tick in Notio.

Anybody can find a bot by its name, so Notio itself picks out whom to listen to: the account that sent the code. Notio keeps the number of that Telegram account, not its name: a new name or @name does not change it. The code works ten minutes and burns after five wrong tries, so it cannot be guessed. The bot does not answer others at all, not even with a no; how many wrote is shown here. Also forbid groups for your bot: in @BotFather send /setjoingroups, choose the bot, then Disable. Unbind forgets the account and gives a new code.
Keep the chat after a restart

The chat is kept in the base of Notio on this computer, encrypted together with the notes, and is not in backups or sync. The newest 500 messages stay. The model remembers the last 20 messages of the chat, so a deleted message is forgotten by it too. Turn this off and the kept chat is deleted.
All messages of the chat will be deleted, and this cannot be undone. The notes and the journal of the assistant stay: what it changed can still be rolled back there.

Code of this Notio for the bot

Your bot program reads Telegram, and Notio connects to it with this code. 1) In the bot, the admin opens /admin, then Notio, then Enter a code of Notio, and sends this code. 2) Here press Check: the name of the bot appears. 3) A person writes to the bot /notio and this code, then /n and a request; /n_undo rolls back, /n_yes confirms. 4) The person appears below: tick them to allow. The address is the one of the program: on this computer http://127.0.0.1:8790; on a home network or VPN, the address of that computer. Between Notio and the program the words go unencrypted, so only on your own computer or network.
